## 从文件读取到设备消费的硬件路径

第一步，清单与索引把逻辑对象映射到固定文件及范围；布局不相容时生成转换计划。第二步，缓冲路径可能从页缓存满足读取，mmap 可能因缺页进入存储路径，直接 I/O 则按具体合同读取用户缓冲。一个逻辑范围可以拆成多个物理请求，多次相邻逻辑读取也可能合并。

第三步，[Linux blk-mq 文档](../sources/S-LINUX-IO.md)区分软件暂存队列与硬件派发队列。能够走最短路径的请求可以直接送往硬件；需要合并或 I/O scheduler 处理时进入软件队列。相邻 sector 可在适用队列内合并，scheduler 可以重排以改善公平或性能；不能假定任意不同软件队列都能合并。硬件无法接受时，请求保留在待派发列表。块层用 tag 匹配驱动完成，块层和设备协议均不保证提交顺序就是完成顺序。

第四步，应用按文件、范围、尝试和 lease 重建完成集合。块层 tag 不是永久对象身份，不能把它跨复用周期直接当作模型版本。必需源范围齐备、相关写者终结且错误已处理后，CPU 转换读取源、写入目标表示；随后 H2D DMA 读取主机目标并写入设备输入。主机源必须保护到 DMA 实际读完，设备输入保护到 kernel 最后读取。

第五步，复制完成和消费者执行通过实际覆盖这些操作的 stream/event 或其他平台关系连接。某个 host API 返回、某个外层 event 被记录，不能独自证明库内部所有 stream 已完成。硬件能并发不等于该负载一定重叠，合法依赖也不等于共享资源足够。

[ServerlessLLM](../sources/S-SERVERLESSLLM.md) §4.2 将固定大小块池、直接文件访问、锁页内存、层内并行读取与层间任务队列组合起来；线程把已读块的 offset/size 交给下一层。论文报告的是该系统的数据路径与测试床，不证明所有 mmap、直接 I/O、锁页或线程组织都具有相同表现。

## 外部 DMA 直达 GPU 的边界

绕过主机 staging 是另一条设计轴。[GPUDirect RDMA 固定文档](../sources/S-GPUDIRECT.md)把存储适配器列为第三方设备示例，但这不等于普通文件读取自动支持设备内存。所述路径需要第三方驱动、GPU 分配类型、注册与 BAR 映射相容，并满足 PCIe 拓扑和平台条件。固定文档要求共享上游 PCIe root complex，IOMMU 不执行非 1:1 地址翻译；即使拓扑满足，具体平台仍可能受芯片组或驱动限制。

pin 与注册可能达到毫秒级，因此可通过 lazy unpinning 或 registration cache 摊销。缓存必须检测分配撤销和地址复用，不能只按虚拟地址命中。固定文档还要求相应 CUDA 内存操作一致性注册，例如按其合同设置整分配的 SYNC_MEMOPS；这会限制某些优化，也有成本。映射撤销回调需要清除引用并等待外部 DMA，不能在持锁回调中等待 GPU 做其他工作而形成死锁。

内存顺序是独立条件。§2.7 说明：GPU 对 GPUDirect 操作的观察顺序由 CPU 发起的 CUDA 同步或工作提交 API 建立。所需 DMA 写必须先相对于将提交依赖工作的 CPU 线程完成，再由该线程发起依赖 CUDA 工作。仅有设备发出事务、稍后的主机读回，或一组看起来递增的时间戳，都不能补上这条因果边。

一条合法的抽象路径是：分配与映射有效→外部 DMA 写→提交线程取得完成保证→后续 CUDA 提交→依赖 kernel。若 kernel 已经与该 DMA 写并发读取同一范围，固定文档允许它读到旧值、部分值或乱序值；稍后读回新值不能追溯修复这个读取。unpin 还必须晚于相关外部 DMA 完成；释放 GPU 分配则另需等待所有 GPU 使用者，两个释放条件不能混同。

直通可以省去该路径原有的主机 staging 及其流量，但不会消除存储 IOPS、排队、校验和表示转换。若转换仍是主项，或准备成本无法摊销，端到端时间未必降低。本章没有存储直通、GPUDirect Storage 或 GPUDirect RDMA 的目标机实测，不能从映射和顺序合同推导吞吐提升。

## 有限流水、容量与组合轨迹

在各阶段独立、各阶段单服务者按块顺序处理、缓冲足够且无其他跨块依赖时，第 i 块第 k 阶段完成时间为 F[i,k]=max(F[i−1,k],F[i,k−1])+t[i,k]，不存在的前驱取零。对各块阶段时间相同的 N 块，T_0=0，N≥1 时 T_N=Σ_k t_k+(N−1)max_k t_k。第一块仍支付依赖阶段之和，最后一块仍要排空。

该递推不包含有限槽等待。采用整组保留到最后消费的 S 个槽组，按块顺序接纳、各阶段 FIFO 时，第零阶段还要等待 F[i−S,last]，因此把它加入 max 的前驱即可得到这个特定方案的有限容量参考。若各池分别释放，则应按各池最后使用者建立不同边，不能沿用整组方案的释放关系。

固定周期 P、固定生存期 L_j、同刻结束后可以立即复用时，池 j 至少需要 ceil(L_j/P) 个槽。L=9 ms、P=4 ms 时需要 3 槽；只有 2 槽会让在 8 ms 启动的块覆盖到 9 ms 才结束的块。相邻 [0,4)、[4,8) 可以复用一个槽。长度可变、乱序、预留早于实际开始或取消排空时，不能用平均 L 保证安全；实际回收仍由最后访问控制。

设定四阶段分别耗 8、3、2、5 ms。四块在独立资源、充足缓冲下于 42 ms 完成，完全串行为 72 ms。对七块，理想流水为 66 ms。采用前述保守槽组，每组同时预留主机源、转换输出和设备输入，有限事件模型与增加容量边的参考递推得到：

| 槽组数 | 七块完成时间 | 三种等大缓冲的显式容量 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 126 ms | 3b |
| 2 | 72 ms | 6b |
| 3 | 66 ms | 9b |

这是规定资源和释放方案下的模型结果，不是硬件测量。更多槽在此条件下可以解除等待，达到慢阶段限制后则不能继续缩短周期。若缩短某池的持有时间，容量和时序都要按新方案重

# K-SYS-019：部署环境：版本契约、可见设备与真实资源边界

部署描述必须能够解释模型实际运行在哪些资源上。镜像、宿主内核/驱动、设备暴露、用户态库、CPU/内存限制、文件与网络路径共同决定可执行性和性能。容器能够启动，不代表这些条件已经形成有效的推理环境。

## 环境身份与相容关系

记录模型制品、执行器和编译器版本，用户态计算/通信库，宿主驱动与内核，以及实际设备能力。兼容关系按目标平台的固定文档和验证确定，不能由版本号大小或某个历史 README 的最低要求推断所有组合都可用。编译缓存还需绑定目标能力和相关编译条件；拷贝已编译文件不保证另一类设备能执行。

镜像携带的用户态依赖与宿主提供的设备驱动、设备文件和资源控制属于不同层。问题可能表现为设备完全不可见、库初始化失败、某个 kernel 路径不支持，或通信路径降为另一种传输。应记录实际选择，不能只写“使用 GPU”或“启用 RDMA”。

[NVIDIA device plugin v0.16.1](../sources/S-NVIDIA-PLUGIN.md) 显示设备清单可以经环境变量、挂载或 CDI 方式交给容器运行时，且设备身份有 UUID/index 选择。这说明部署分配、容器可见性与执行器里的逻辑序号需要形成映射。重启后逻辑 device 0 仍叫 0，不证明仍是之前那张物理卡或同一 MIG 资源。

## CPU、内存与拓扑限制

CPU 线程池大小需要结合实际可用 CPU 集与带宽 quota。设宿主有 64 个逻辑 CPU，但该服务的 CPU 预算为每 100 ms 最多消耗 200 ms 执行时间，长期上限相当于 2 个 CPU 的时间；把线程池设成 64 不会获得 64 核持续计算。[Linux cgroup v2](../sources/S-LINUX-RESOURCES.md) 还规定限制沿层级收紧，子组设置不能突破祖先限制。

若设定分词每请求消耗 10 ms CPU、其他主机工作消耗 6 ms CPU，150 请求/s 需要 2.4 CPU 秒/s，已超出上述 2 CPU 预算。即使 GPU 很空闲，也不能先推断模型 kernel 是瓶颈。需要测 cpu.stat 的节流、实际队列和线程时间，并考虑增大主机份额或减少主机工作。

内存预算包含匿名缓冲、文件缓存、共享内存和相关内核资源。设加载时源权重 24 GiB、转换后权重 24 GiB、staging 4 GiB 同时存活，则主项为 52 GiB；宿主拥有 512 GiB 也无法使一个上限 48 GiB 的服务自动加载成功。可采用已验证的流式转换降低峰值，或调整合法资源配额。

cpuset 的 CPU 与内存节点设置、实际 NUMA 分配、NIC/SSD/GPU 亲和共同决定数据路径。指定核集合并不自动保证页面已在期望节点；改变内存节点可能触发昂贵且不完全的页面迁移。部署验证应读取有效值和实际路径，而不是只保留期望配置。

## 健康、就绪与可接收容量

健康探测回答进程是否能够推进其必要工作；就绪探测回答该模型版本和执行组是否已满足接收契约。端口能连接、HTTP 返回成功或插件进程没有退出，都不能单独证明权重完成加载、通信组完整、设备可用和代表路径正确。

就绪还可以有资源范围：允许短文本但尚未准备长图像路径，或者 KV 已满而需要暂停准入。若把暂时过载当成进程失效并不断重启，就会清空热状态、重复加载并放大存储压力。无法恢复的设备或执行组错误则应退出相应可用集合，按[恢复](serving-recovery.md)协议重建。

共享内存容量、文件描述符、进程/线程限制、I/O 限额和网络访问范围也需要进入环境检查。只提升 GPU 数量可能同时增加 tokenizer 进程、IPC 缓冲和并发制品读取，从而先耗尽这些资源。限制的数值要绑定实际配置，不在知识正文中写成通用默认值。

## 更新与独立验证

更换驱动、设备插件或运行时可能影响整个节点，而不只是一个服务进程。固定插件文档明确建议更新插件前排空 GPU 任务，并不保证任务在滚动升级中存活。具体升级策略应由目标版本与设备支持决定，先停止新准入，再完成或迁移已有工作，确认最后访问结束后释放旧环境。

验收分三层：核对真实环境身份与有效资源；运行覆盖目标 shape、dtype、通信与状态路径的最小模型参考；重放代表负载验证服务质量和资源峰值。再测试 CPU 限额收紧、加载超出主存、设备映射变化、部分 rank 未就绪和实例排空。每次失败都应能区分环境不相容、配置不足与实现错误。

当任务只在单一受控机器运行时，直接部署可以减少组织成本；多租户、多版本与弹性环境需要更明确的资源和生命周期契约。无论部署载体是什么，实验都要在与目标一致的有效资源范围内比较，避免把环境改变当成内核优化收益。

# K-MODEL-014：视觉识别与卷积：空间布局、预处理与任务输出

视觉识别的请求从图像字节开始，经过确定的几何和颜色变换、卷积或视觉编码器，再产生分类、检测等任务输出。空间分辨率、布局与预后处理会改变模型函数和资源成本，不能用生成式模型的输入 token 数直接代替。

## 原始图像到模型张量的契约

解码器、颜色通道顺序、值域、方向、resize 插值、裁剪或 letterbox、归一化与布局共同定义输入。训练时随机增强不能直接作为确定推理的默认行为。改变 resize、中心裁剪或多视图测试，是改变实际输入/评估方案；仅比较相同模型名称不足以证明公平。

输入可采用 NCHW、NHWC 或分块通道布局。逻辑索引相同不代表物理 stride 相同；转换布局需要真实读取和写入，若每层来回变换，可能抵消单个卷积 kernel 的优势。batch 中混合分辨率时，padding 与有效区域的含义必须贯穿后续计算。卷积会读取局部邻域，简单补零后再对有效像素裁切输出，也未必等同于独立处理原图，尤其涉及池化、全局统计或边界传播时。

视觉 encoder 若采用 patch/attention，应按实际模型处理位置和网格；本章的卷积成本公式不适用于所有视觉网络。视觉识别、视觉语言模型的图像编码阶段与图像生成的去噪循环也有不同任务输出和状态。

## 卷积的计算与中间表示

设 batch 为 B，输入 Cin 个通道，输出 Cout 个通道，卷积核 Kh×Kw，组数 G，输出空间 Hout×Wout。乘加数为 B Hout Wout Cout (Cin/G) Kh Kw；若一次乘加计两次浮点操作，FLOPs 为其两倍。stride、padding 和 dilation 决定输出形状，不能把它们只当作性能参数。

直接卷积按空间邻域加载；显式 im2col 将输入窗口展开成矩阵，再执行 GEMM，改善规则计算却可能产生大临时区；隐式 GEMM 在读取时构造逻辑窗口，避免完整展开，但增加索引和边界处理。Winograd/FFT 等变换路线有各自适用形状、额外变换和数值条件；仅凭卷积核大小不能假定目标 backend 已选中某条路线。

1×1 卷积、深度可分离卷积和普通 3×3 卷积的复用不同。depthwise 降低计算，却也降低算术强度，可能更受访存和提交限制。应分别记录权重、输入/输出、中间工作区、布局转换与 epilogue，而不是用统一峰值算力预测全部层。

## 残差、归一化与合法融合

ResNet 固定论文中的残差块将 F(x) 与 x 或投影 W_s x 相加，再按相应结构激活。两支必须有相同空间形状和通道解释；降采样位置与 shortcut 形式是 checkpoint 契约。相加前 x 仍活跃，原地覆盖它会破坏后面的 shortcut，即使顺序执行没有并发也会出错。

固定推理统计的 BatchNorm 是按通道的仿射变换。对于卷积 y=W*x+b，令 a=γ/√(variance+ε)，可以构造 W′=aW、b′=a(b−mean)+β。这个代数合并要求统计和参数固定，并与实际精度/舍入相容；若运行中仍计算 batch 统计，则不能用同一常量折叠。量化后的 scale、bias 和饱和位置也需重新核对。

卷积、bias、固定 BN、激活的融合可减少中间写读；残差 add 融合还要满足另一输入的生命周期、布局与 dtype。融合改变归约或舍入次序时，使用允许误差与任务质量验证。更多融合也可能增加寄存器、工作区或限制库调用，不能保证端到端单调变快。

## 分类与检测是不同输出链

分类路径通常经过特征提取、pooling 和分类头，返回类别分数及其映射。单标签 softmax、多标签 sigmoid、top-k 与阈值策略必须遵循任务定义。类别表版本和输出顺序属于结果身份。

ResNet v1 附录 A–C 给出一个具体检测路线：整图共享卷积特征，经 proposal 网络产生候选区域，再做 RoI pooling、区域级计算、分类与框回归；后续可加入 box refinement、NMS 和多尺度。这里的候选数、RoI 形状和后处理带来数据相关工作。该历史实现支撑机制说明，不把其固定阈值或 proposal 数当作所有检测器的默认配置。

检测输出必须带回原图坐标。resize 比例、padding、crop 偏移、坐标格式、边界是否包含末端以及 NMS 的同分顺序都要统一。对框先裁剪再做 IoU，与先 NMS 后裁剪可能不同；某些流程可以合法使用不同顺序，但必须与参考定义一致。分类正确不能代替定位正确，最终指标应包含相应 IoU 条件下的 AP/mAP。

## 请求执行与资源放置

CPU 解码/预处理、设备搬运、GPU 执行、CPU/GPU 后处理可以分阶段聚批，但需要携带图像 ID、几何变换及有效输出范围。一个阶段 batch 大小最优，不意味着完整请求适合等待同样大的批。解码和 NMS 可能成为 CPU 瓶颈，长分辨率或候选数多的请求也会拖长尾部。

异步流水中，输入图像缓冲、转换后张量、模型工作区和输出各有最后消费者。取消只移除客户端结果需求，不代表设备已停止读写。图捕获和编译分桶可以管理有限分辨率与 proposal 容量，超出容量应明确换路径，不能静默裁掉对象以保持固定 shape。

## C12-C：视觉识别与检测的完整验证场景

设定一个固定 checkpoint、224×224 单裁剪分类契约，并考察其中一层 B=1、56×56、Cin=Cout=64、3×3、G=1、stride=1、保持空间尺寸的卷积。其乘加数为 56²×64×64×9=115,605,504；FP16 输出为 401,408 字节。显式 im2col 的输入展开有 56²×(64×9) 个元素，即 3,612,672 字节，约为原输入的 9 倍，尚未计 GEMM 工作区。换成 depthwise 是不同算子，其乘加仅 1,806,336，不能在未改变模型的优化比较中直接替换。

候选 A 保持统一布局并用库卷积，候选 B 使用有目标 shape 依据的编译/融合路径。两者以相同图像字节、前处理和权重执行，先比较解码后像素、卷积边界、残差输出和最终 logits，再比较固定测试集 top-1/top-5。测试纯色、单像素脉冲、非整除通道、非连续 stride、极小图、不同宽高比与混合批，定位插值、边界和布局错误。

检测子场景固定一个有完整任务头的模型及其 resize/NMS 规则。用可手算矩形验证坐标映射与 IoU：A=[0,0,2,2]、B=[1,0,3,2]，采用连续坐标面积，交集 2、并集 6，IoU=1/3；是否抑制由既定阈值和比较

# K-MODEL-016：图模型推理：邻居依赖、采样与不规则执行

图模型推理由目标节点向外展开计算依赖，再把邻居特征逐层聚合到目标。请求数量相同，不代表边数、特征读取量或计算量相同；节点度分布、重复邻居与图的版本直接影响执行。

## 图、特征和聚合器组成输入函数

模型输入至少包括节点/边身份、方向与类型、特征 schema 和版本、邻域定义、采样规则及模型参数。一个节点 ID 不能脱离图命名空间解释，特征更新也不能与旧邻接快照任意混配。若任务有时间边界，只允许看到该时点之前的数据，未来边进入缓存同样是输入错误。

GraphSAGE 固定论文给出递归机制：第 k 层对选定邻居的第 k−1 层表示聚合，再与自身表示拼接，经线性变换、激活和规定的归一化得到新表示。均值、max-pooling 和 LSTM 聚合是不同模型；均值/逐元素 max 对邻居排列具有数学不变性，LSTM 聚合依赖顺序，随机排列只是其训练/执行约定，不能把它当作严格集合不变算子。

自身节点是否纳入邻域、是拼接还是一同平均、空邻域怎样定义、归一化零向量如何处理，都需要从实际模型确定。GraphSAGE 的均值拼接与 GCN 风格的统一均值也不同，不能仅凭二者都“聚合邻居”替换权重接口。

## 依赖展开与特征收集

给定目标集合 B_K，反向确定每层所需集合 B_{k−1}=B_k∪N_k(B_k)，再从第 0 层向前计算。一个中间节点的第 k 层表示只有在其全部被选择的第 k−1 层依赖就绪后才能生成。仅沿目标节点收集最外层邻居，忽略自身分支所需的中间表示，会得到不完整的计算图。

同一层、同一图/特征版本、同一采样定义下，重复节点的特征读取可以去重，并通过映射恢复每条边的消费关系。对于边权、平行边或按出现次数聚合的函数，去重读取不等于去重语义。跨层表示也不能只按节点 ID 合并，因为它们包含的邻域深度不同。

CSR/邻接列表等表示决定边遍历与行定位成本。收集节点后可重排为更连续的特征访问，并记录反向映射；聚合结果仍需回到正确目标。CPU 采样、GPU gather/聚合与远端特征读取可以流水，但边索引、特征、当前批映射和临时输出均需明确在途所有权。

## 采样是质量与资源之间的选择

全邻域执行给定图和参数的确定函数；固定 fanout 限制读取与工作量，通常改变结果。一个无偏的邻居均值估计，经过激活、归一化和多层递归后也不自动产生无偏预测，更不保证与全邻域分类相同。必须把采样近似与低精度实现误差分开评价。

邻居不足 fanout 时，有放回、无放回、padding 或全取等不同策略。用重复节点补齐会改变均值的权重，除非有配套计数/屏蔽规则。采样种子和邻居遍历顺序要可追溯；复用采样结果可减少开销，但减少随机覆盖并绑定图版本。

GraphSAGE v1 的实验还对度数做了预处理截断，其报告的效率和质量不能直接理解为在任意完整原图上的保证。论文的表达能力证明是存在某些参数的结论，也不构成一个给定 checkpoint 在采样图上保持质量的证明。

## 算术、带宽和分片账

若每层最大采样数为 s_k，则依赖集合有上界 |B_{k−1}|≤|B_k|(1+s_k)。这个上界包含自身路径；重复邻居和低度节点会使实际集合更小。实际采样边数、唯一节点数、缓存命中与读取字节应分别记录，不能只报告目标 batch。

输入特征字节约为 U d₀ s，其中 U 为本批实际读取的唯一节点数；缓存行、索引、通信封装和远端访问会增加流量。均值聚合主要随采样边数×输入维度增长，线性层则随需计算节点数×输入/输出维度增长。先聚合再线性或先线性再聚合，只在函数、线性性和数值条件允许时等价；存在非线性、边特定权重或不同自身变换时不能任意交换。

按节点分片能将其特征和邻接放在一起，但跨分区边引入远端特征读取。复制边界特征可减少通信并增加容量与失效维护；度数或热点偏斜会让均匀节点数的分片仍极不均衡。缓存完整多层 embedding 还依赖其邻域，当边或底层特征更新时，影响可沿层数传播；只更新被直接修改节点的最终结果未必足够。

## C12-E：采样图推理的完整验证场景

设定两层模型，输出目标 B₂=64；输出层每节点取至多 10 个邻居，输入层为其所需节点各取至多 5 个邻居。包含自身分支时，|B₁|≤64×11=704，|B₀|≤704×6=4,224；最多采样边数为 64×10+704×5=4,160。若输入为 128 维 FP32，最外层唯一特征读取上界是 4,224×128×4=2,162,688 字节，即 2.0625 MiB，另有邻接、映射、层间表示和输出。共享邻居可以降低实际值，但必须由本批去重统计确认。

候选 A 在图和特征可容纳时做全邻域、按层批处理；候选 B 做有明确规则的固定 fanout 采样，并把特征收集与 GPU 执行流水。A 可作为给定图函数的数值参考，B 是质量约束下的近似候选，不能用相同输出要求把合法采样差异误判为 kernel bug，也不能忽略它对任务质量的影响。

先验证同一冻结采样子图在单线程参考与优化实现上的结果。独立一层算例规定自身 x_v=2、邻居值 4 和 8，均值聚合得 6；拼接后使用权重 (1,1)、ReLU，归一化之前结果为 8。只采样邻居 4 时为 6，清楚显示采样改变函数。若模型还含归一化，应继续执行并分别比较前后值，不能借最终归一化掩盖中间聚合错误。

覆盖孤立节点、重复边、自环、入边/出边反转、零特征、邻居不足、共享邻居、超高度节点、多个图同名 ID、图更新中的请求以及远端特征缺失。对均值/max 模型做邻居排列不变测试；对 LSTM 聚合则固定其顺序契约。采样质量用多种种子和图分布测节点分类 F1/accuracy 或任务指定指标，报告均值与波动，并与全邻域和训练时预处理相匹配的参考分别比较。

性能从请求进入到所有目标结果返回，拆分采样、ID 路由、特征获取、搬运、聚合、线性计算和结果重排，同时报告目标节点/s、实际边/s、字节与 p99。缓存热启动、重复查询和全冷特征应分开。图较小且更新少时，全图预计算/按层执行可能更有效；节点零散、图很大或时限较紧时，采样与局部缓存才可能获益。更新频率和质量要求提高时，缓存及采样策略都需要重新选择。

## 来源与推导

- [S-GRAPHSAGE：Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs](../sources/S-GRAPHSAGE.md)：固定 v1 给出邻居采样、均值/pooling/LSTM 聚合与逐层表示，包含 minibatch 依赖、图数据预处理、实验和

# K-SYS-025：已知张力：单实例交互式服务中的机制冲突

单实例交互式生成服务里，若干机制在同一资源与同一时延预算上相互拉扯。下列条目是有来源支撑的探索起点：各写机制、来源指针、可观测信号与反转条件。清单不穷尽，也不构成任务必须处理的缺陷列表。

## Decode 带宽下界与 ITL

机制：每轮 decode 若读取大块权重与各请求可见 KV，则设备主存流量给出迭代时间下界；客户端 ITL 还要覆盖主机、采样、同步与排队。当流量下界已接近或超过目标 ITL，继续堆叠同轮工作只会恶化间隔，吞吐与单请求间隔不能用同一除法解释。

来源指针：[容量与 roofline](../hardware/memory-and-roofline.md) 中权重/KV 流量分解；[ORCA](../sources/S-ORCA.md) 的迭代批语义说明一轮推进多个请求仍共享同轮等待。

可观测：活跃 decode 数增加时，每请求输出间隔近似不降或上升，而设备 HBM 字节/迭代接近表征带宽×时间；主机空闲比例高。

反转：权重驻留被更高层缓存命中、KV 读取因共享或压缩真实下降、目标 ITL 放宽，或阶段分离使本实例不再承担该流量形态时，张力缓解或形态改变。

## Prefill 与 Decode 干扰

机制：长 prefill 的大矩阵与长上下文 attention 占用 SM、HBM 与工作区；与短 query decode 同实例交错时，decode 的迭代被拉长，表现为已有流式用户的 ITL 尖峰。分块把 prefill 切成可调度片，但每块仍须按可见性读取其依赖的历史，块长受剩余 ITL 预算约束，不是任意变小就无代价。

来源指针：[SARATHI](../sources/S-SARATHI.md)；[分块 Prefill](../algorithms/chunked-prefill.md)。

可观测：新长大请求到达后，无关会话的 token 间隔同步变差；时间线上出现长 prefill kernel 与 decode 交替，decode 间隙被拉宽；TTFT 改善若来自抢占 decode，常伴随 ITL 恶化。

反转：prefill/decode 分实例且状态迁移成本可接受、到达以短输入为主、或时间片与准入使 decode 预算硬隔离时，同实例干扰下降。分实例引入的传输与调度是另一组成本。

## 投机收益随 Batch 增大而消失

机制：投机用草稿成本换目标并行验证；单位已确认 token 成本须低于普通目标 decode。连续批摊薄每 token 权重读取后，普通 decode 变便宜，同一 γ 与草稿配置可能从加速变为减速；额外验证 token 还占用其他请求预算。

来源指针：[投机解码](../algorithms/speculation-budget.md)；[S-SPEC](../sources/S-SPEC.md)。设定算例见该章：普通每 token 10 单位、投机后 8 单位有益；普通降至 6 单位后同配置变慢。

可观测：小批或单请求加速比明显，批增大后接受长度未变但端到端 token/s 低于关闭投机；验证占用的 token 预算挤出其他就绪请求。

反转：批变小、草稿更准或更便宜、验证与 decode 能重叠且不挤占关键资源，或普通路径因别的原因变慢时，投机可再次有利。关闭投机是合法运行点。

## KV 量化的质量悬崖

机制：降低 KV 位宽削减驻留与部分流量，但误差经注意力传播；分组轴、尺度与残余区配置在某些位宽/模型/任务上出现断崖式质量下降，而不是平滑可插值的曲线。容量账按理想位宽估算会忽略 scale、残余与 workspace。

来源指针：[KIVI](../sources/S-KIVI.md) §3–4 与适用边界；[量化契约](../algorithms/quantization-contract.md)。

可观测：某位宽下任务指标相对基线突然恶化，相邻更高位宽仍接近基线；仅测 TTFT/首 token 正常，长生成后偏离；消费压缩历史的 decode 与仍用高精度缓存的 prefill 结果不一致。

反转：换分组轴或残余策略、提高关键层精度、任务对误差不敏感，或长度/批使流量不再主导时，可重新评估。悬崖位置随模型与任务移动，不能当跨模型常数。

## 图桶、Workspace 与 KV 争容量

机制：CUDA Graph 与固定计划缓冲需要稳定地址与多桶驻留；注意力/矩阵 workspace、流水双缓冲同样占用设备容量。它们与 KV 争同一显存池：桶与 workspace 增大可降提交与峰值临时，却直接减少可驻留历史或并发。

来源指针：[CUDA Graph 缓冲](../frameworks/cuda-graph-buffers.md)；[内存分配器](../system-semantics/memory-allocators.md)；[S-TORCH-CUDA](../sources/S-TORCH-CUDA.md)。

可观测：启用更多图桶或更大 workspace 后，最大并发或最大上下文下降；OOM/驱逐与“计算变快”同时出现；页回收成功但图仍引用旧代次导致错误。

反转：形状集合收窄使桶数下降、改为 eager 且提交不是关键路径、或扩容设备内存时，争用缓和。地址不稳定的负载下图路径本身可能先失效。

## 小 Batch 下主机侧占比

机制：设备迭代很短时，分词、调度、采样、JSON/协议与 launch 的主机时间在端到端中占比上升。优化仅针对 HBM 或 GEMM 时，壁钟改善受 Amdahl 限制；图与异步可摊薄提交，但不消除采样与协议成本。

来源指针：[主机运行时](../system-semantics/host-runtime.md)；[CUDA 执行中的 eager/图](../hardware/cuda-execution.md)；[S-NSYS](../sources/S-NSYS.md) 对 host/device 时间线边界的说明。

可观测：设备利用率低但 ITL 仍高；时间线显示 kernel 很短、host 线程或运行时跨度占间隔大部分；增大批后设备占比上升、主机占比下降。

反转：批变大、输出更长使设备工作占优，或主机路径与设备重叠且无假同步时，张力形态改变。主机变快不自动提高已饱和的 HBM 路径。

## 张力之间的耦合

上述条目常耦合：为缓解带宽–ITL 而增大批，可能削弱投机；为保护 ITL 而切细 prefill，可能增加 launch 与主机占比；为省 KV 而量化，可能撞上质量悬崖；为降提交而加图桶，可能挤掉并发。要区分单因

===== specs/www.rst =====
====================================
HTTP & WebSocket ASGI Message Format
====================================

**Version**: 2.5 (2024-06-05)

The HTTP+WebSocket ASGI sub-specification outlines how to transport HTTP/1.1,
HTTP/2 and WebSocket connections within ASGI.

It is deliberately intended and designed to be a superset of the WSGI format
and specifies how to translate between the two for the set of requests that
are able to be handled by WSGI.


Spec Versions
-------------

This spec has had the following versions:

* ``2.0``: The first version of the spec, released with ASGI 2.0
* ``2.1``: Added the ``headers`` key to the WebSocket Accept response
* ``2.2``: Allow ``None`` in the second item of ``server`` scope value.
* ``2.3``: Added the ``reason`` key to the WebSocket close event.
* ``2.4``: Calling ``send()`` on a closed connection should raise an error
* ``2.5``: Added the ``reason`` key to the WebSocket disconnect event.

Spec versions let you understand what the server you are using understands. If
a server tells you it only supports version ``2.0`` of this spec, then
sending ``headers`` with a WebSocket Accept message is an error, for example.

They are separate from the HTTP version or the ASGI version.


HTTP
----

The HTTP format covers HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, as the changes in
HTTP/2 are largely on the transport level. A protocol server should give
different scopes to different requests on the same HTTP/2 connection, and
correctly multiplex the responses back to the same stream in which they came.
The HTTP version is available as a string in the scope.

Multiple header fields with the same name are complex in HTTP. RFC 7230
states that for any header field that can appear multiple times, it is exactly
equivalent to sending that header field only once with all the values joined by
commas.

However, for HTTP cookies (``Cookie`` and ``Set-Cookie``) the allowed behaviour
does not follow the above rule, and also varies slightly based on the HTTP
protocol version:

* For the ``Set-Cookie`` header in HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP2.0, it may appear
  repeatedly, but cannot be concatenated by commas (or anything else) into a
  single header field.

* For the ``Cookie`` header, in HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1, RFC 7230 and RFC 6265
  make it clear that the ``Cookie`` header must only be sent once by a
  user-agent, and must be concatenated into a single octet string using the
  two-octet delimiter of 0x3b, 0x20 (the ASCII string "; "). However in HTTP/2,
  RFC 9113 states that ``Cookie`` headers MAY appear repeatedly, OR be
  concatenated using the two-octet delimiter of 0x3b, 0x20
  (the ASCII string "; ").

The ASGI design decision is to transport both request and response headers as
lists of 2-element ``[name, value]`` lists and preserve headers exactly as they
were provided.

For ASGI applications that support HTTP/2, care should be taken to handle the
special case for ``Cookie`` noted above.

The HTTP protocol should be signified to ASGI applications with a ``type``
value of ``http``.


HTTP Connection Scope
'''''''''''''''''''''

HTTP connections have a single-request *connection scope* - that is, your
application will be called at the start of the request, and will last until
the end of that specific request, even if the underlying socket is still open
and serving multiple requests.

If you hold a response open for long-polling or similar, the *connection scope*
will persist until the response closes from either the client or server side.

The *connection scope* information passed in ``scope`` contains:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"http"``.

* ``asgi["version"]`` (*Unicode string*) -- Version of the ASGI spec.

* ``asgi["spec_version"]`` (*Unicode string*) -- Version of the ASGI
  HTTP spec this server understands; for example: ``"2.0"``, ``"2.1"``, ``"2.2"``,
  etc. Optional; if missing assume ``"2.0"``.

* ``http_version`` (*Unicode string*) -- One of ``"1.0"``, ``"1.1"`` or ``"2"``.

* ``method`` (*Unicode string*) -- The HTTP method name, uppercased.

* ``scheme`` (*Unicode string*) -- URL scheme portion (likely ``"http"`` or
  ``"https"``). Optional (but must not be empty); default is ``"http"``.

* ``path`` (*Unicode string*) -- HTTP request target excluding any query
  string, with percent-encoded sequences and UTF-8 byte sequences
  decoded into characters.

* ``raw_path`` (*byte string*) -- The original HTTP path component,
  excluding any query string, unmodified from the bytes that were
  received by the web server. Some web server implementations may
  be unable to provide this. Optional; if missing defaults to ``None``.

* ``query_string`` (*byte string*) -- URL portion after the ``?``,
  percent-encoded.

* ``root_path`` (*Unicode string*) -- The root path this application
  is mounted at; same as ``SCRIPT_NAME`` in WSGI. Optional; if missing
  defaults to ``""``.

* ``headers`` (*Iterable[[byte string, byte string]]*) -- An iterable of
  ``[name, value]`` two-item iterables, where ``name`` is the header name, and
  ``value`` is the header value. Order of header values must be preserved from
  the original HTTP request; order of header names is not important. Duplicates
  are possible and must be preserved in the message as received. Header names
  should be lowercased, but it is not required; servers should preserve header case
  on a best-effort basis. Pseudo headers (present in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3) must be
  removed; if ``:authority`` is present its value must be added to the start of
  the iterable with ``host`` as the header name or replace any existing host
  header already present.

* ``client`` (*Iterable[Unicode string, int]*) -- A two-item iterable
  of ``[host, port]``, where ``host`` is the remote host's IPv4 or
  IPv6 address, and ``port`` is the remote port as an
  integer. Optional; if missing defaults to ``None``.

* ``server`` (*Iterable[Unicode string, Optional[int]]*) -- Either a
  two-item iterable of ``[host, port]``, where ``host`` is the
  listening address for this server, and ``port`` is the integer
  listening port, or ``[path, None]`` where ``path`` is that of the
  unix socket. Optional; if missing defaults to ``None``.

* ``state`` Optional(*dict[Unicode string, Any]*) -- A copy of the
  namespace passed into the lifespan corresponding to this request. (See :doc:`lifespan`).
  Optional; if missing the server does not support this feature.

Servers are responsible for handling inbound and outbound chunked transfer
encodings. A request with a ``chunked`` encoded body should be automatically
de-chunked by the server and presented to the application as plain body bytes;
a response that is given to the server with no ``Content-Length`` may be chunked
as the server sees fit.


Request - ``receive`` event
'''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent to the application to indicate an incoming request. Most of the request
information is in the connection ``scope``; the body message serves as a way to
stream large incoming HTTP bodies in chunks, and as a trigger to actually run
request code (as you should not trigger on a connection opening alone).

Note that if the request is being sent using ``Transfer-Encoding: chunked``,
the server is responsible for handling this encoding. The ``http.request``
messages should contain just the decoded contents of each chunk.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"http.request"``.

* ``body`` (*byte string*) -- Body of the request. Optional; if
  missing defaults to ``b""``. If ``more_body`` is set, treat as start
  of body and concatenate on further chunks.

* ``more_body`` (*bool*) -- Signifies if there is additional content
  to come (as part of a Request message). If ``True``, the consuming
  application should wait until it gets a chunk with this set to
  ``False``. If ``False``, the request is complete and should be
  processed. Optional; if missing defaults to ``False``.


Response Start - ``send`` event
'''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent by the application to start sending a response to the client. Needs to be
followed by at least one response content message.

Protocol servers *need not* flush the data generated by this event to the
send buffer until the first *Response Body* event is processed.
This may give them more leeway to replace the response with an error response
in case internal errors occur while handling the request.

You may send a ``Transfer-Encoding`` header in this message, but the server
must ignore it. Servers handle ``Transfer-Encoding`` themselves, and may opt
to use ``Transfer-Encoding: chunked`` if the application presents a response
that has no ``Content-Length`` set.

Note that this is not the same as ``Content-Encoding``, which the application
still controls, and which is the appropriate place to set ``gzip`` or other
compression flags.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"http.response.start"``.

* ``status`` (*int*) -- HTTP status code.

* ``headers`` (*Iterable[[byte string, byte string]]*) -- An iterable
  of ``[name, value]`` two-item iterables, where ``name`` is the
  header name, and ``value`` is the header value. Order must be
  preserved in the HTTP response.  Header names must be
  lowercased. Optional; if missing defaults to an empty list. Pseudo
  headers (present in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3) must not be present.

* ``trailers`` (*bool*) -- Signifies if the application will send
  trailers. If ``True``, the server must wait until it receives a
  ``"http.response.trailers"`` message after the *Response Body* event.
  Optional; if missing defaults to ``False``.


Response Body - ``send`` event
''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Continues sending a response to the client. Protocol servers must
flush any data passed to them into the send buffer before returning from a
send call. If ``more_body`` is set to ``False``, and the server is not
expecting *Response Trailers* this will complete the response.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"http.response.body"``.

* ``body`` (*byte string*) -- HTTP body content. Concatenated onto any
  previous ``body`` values sent in this connection scope. Optional; if
  missing defaults to ``b""``.

* ``more_body`` (*bool*) -- Signifies if there is additional content
  to come (as part of a *Response Body* message). If ``False``, and the
  server is not expecting *Response Trailers* response will be taken as
  complete and closed, and any further messages on the channel will be
  ignored. Optional; if missing defaults to ``False``.


Disconnected Client - ``send`` exception
''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''

If ``send()`` is called on a closed connection the server should raise
a server-specific subclass of ``OSError``. This is not guaranteed, however,
especially on older ASGI server implementations (it was introduced in spec
version 2.4).

Applications may catch this exception and do cleanup work before
re-raising it or returning with no exception.

Servers must be prepared to catch this exception if they raised it and
should not log it as an error in their server logs.


Disconnect - ``receive`` event
''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent to the application if receive is called after a response has been
sent or after the HTTP connection has been closed. This is mainly useful
for long-polling, where you may want to trigger cleanup code if the
connection closes early.

Once you have received this event, you should expect future calls to ``send()``
to raise an exception, as described above. However, if you have highly
concurrent code, you may find calls to ``send()`` erroring slightly before you
receive this event.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"http.disconnect"``.


WebSocket
---------

WebSockets share some HTTP details - they have a path and headers - but also
have more state. Again, most of that state is in the ``scope``, which will live
as long as the socket does.

WebSocket protocol servers should handle PING/PONG messages themselves, and
send PING messages as necessary to ensure the connection is alive.

WebSocket protocol servers should handle message fragmentation themselves,
and deliver complete messages to the application.

The WebSocket protocol should be signified to ASGI applications with
a ``type`` value of ``websocket``.


Websocket Connection Scope
''''''''''''''''''''''''''

WebSocket connections' scope lives as long as the socket itself - if the
application dies the socket should be closed, and vice-versa.

The *connection scope* information passed in ``scope`` contains initial connection
metadata (mostly from the HTTP request line and headers):

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket"``.

* ``asgi["version"]`` (*Unicode string*) -- The version of the ASGI spec.

* ``asgi["spec_version"]`` (*Unicode string*) -- Version of the ASGI
  HTTP spec this server understands; one of ``"2.0"``, ``"2.1"``, ``"2.2"`` or
  ``"2.3"``. Optional; if missing assume ``"2.0"``.

* ``http_version`` (*Unicode string*) -- One of ``"1.1"`` or
  ``"2"``. Optional; if missing default is ``"1.1"``.

* ``scheme`` (*Unicode string*) -- URL scheme portion (likely ``"ws"`` or
  ``"wss"``). Optional (but must not be empty); default is ``"ws"``.

* ``path`` (*Unicode string*) -- HTTP request target excluding any query
  string, with percent-encoded sequences and UTF-8 byte sequences
  decoded into characters.

* ``raw_path`` (*byte string*) -- The original HTTP path component,
  excluding any query string, unmodified from the bytes that were
  received by the web server. Some web server implementations may
  be unable to provide this. Optional; if missing defaults to ``None``.

* ``query_string`` (*byte string*) -- URL portion after the
  ``?``. Optional; if missing or ``None`` default is empty string.

* ``root_path`` (*Unicode string*) -- The root path this application is
  mounted at; same as ``SCRIPT_NAME`` in WSGI. Optional; if missing
  defaults to empty string.

* ``headers`` (*Iterable[[byte string, byte string]]*) -- An iterable of
  ``[name, value]`` two-item iterables, where ``name`` is the header name and
  ``value`` is the header value. Order should be preserved from the original
  HTTP request; duplicates are possible and must be preserved in the message
  as received. Header names should be lowercased, but it is not required;
  servers should preserve header case on a best-effort basis.
  Pseudo headers (present in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3) must be removed;
  if ``:authority`` is present its value must be added to the
  start of the iterable with ``host`` as the header name
  or replace any existing host header already present.

* ``client`` (*Iterable[Unicode string, int]*) -- A two-item iterable
  of ``[host, port]``, where ``host`` is the remote host's IPv4 or
  IPv6 address, and ``port`` is the remote port. Optional; if missing
  defaults to ``None``.

* ``server`` (*Iterable[Unicode string, Optional[int]]*) -- Either a
  two-item iterable of ``[host, port]``, where ``host`` is the
  listening address for this server, and ``port`` is the integer
  listening port, or ``[path, None]`` where ``path`` is that of the
  unix socket. Optional; if missing defaults to ``None``.

* ``subprotocols`` (*Iterable[Unicode string]*) -- Subprotocols the
  client advertised. Optional; if missing defaults to empty list.

* ``state`` Optional(*dict[Unicode string, Any]*) -- A copy of the
  namespace passed into the lifespan corresponding to this request. (See :doc:`lifespan`).
  Optional; if missing the server does not support this feature.


Connect - ``receive`` event
'''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent to the application when the client initially opens a connection and is about
to finish the WebSocket handshake.

This message must be responded to with either an *Accept* message
or a *Close* message before the socket will pass ``websocket.receive``
messages. The protocol server must send this message
during the handshake phase of the WebSocket and not complete the handshake
until it gets a reply, returning HTTP status code ``403`` if the connection is
denied.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket.connect"``.


Accept - ``send`` event
'''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent by the application when it wishes to accept an incoming connection.

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket.accept"``.

* ``subprotocol`` (*Unicode string*) -- The subprotocol the server
  wishes to accept. Optional; if missing defaults to ``None``.

* ``headers`` (*Iterable[[byte string, byte string]]*) -- An iterable
  of ``[name, value]`` two-item iterables, where ``name`` is the
  header name, and ``value`` is the header value. Order must be
  preserved in the HTTP response.  Header names must be
  lowercased. Must not include a header named
  ``sec-websocket-protocol``; use the ``subprotocol`` key
  instead. Optional; if missing defaults to an empty list. *Added in
  spec version 2.1*. Pseudo headers (present in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3)
  must not be present.


Receive - ``receive`` event
'''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent to the application when a data message is received from the client.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket.receive"``.

* ``bytes`` (*byte string*) -- The message content, if it was binary
  mode, or ``None``. Optional; if missing, it is equivalent to
  ``None``.

* ``text`` (*Unicode string*) -- The message content, if it was text
  mode, or ``None``. Optional; if missing, it is equivalent to
  ``None``.

Exactly one of ``bytes`` or ``text`` must be non-``None``. One or both
keys may be present, however.


Send - ``send`` event
'''''''''''''''''''''

Sent by the application to send a data message to the client.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket.send"``.

* ``bytes`` (*byte string*) -- Binary message content, or ``None``.
   Optional; if missing, it is equivalent to ``None``.

* ``text`` (*Unicode string*) -- Text message content, or ``None``.
   Optional; if missing, it is equivalent to ``None``.

Exactly one of ``bytes`` or ``text`` must be non-``None``. One or both
keys may be present, however.


.. _disconnect-receive-event-ws:

Disconnect - ``receive`` event
''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent to the application when either connection to the client is lost, either from
the client closing the connection, the server closing the connection, or loss of the
socket.

Once you have received this event, you should expect future calls to ``send()``
to raise an exception, as described below. However, if you have highly
concurrent code, you may find calls to ``send()`` erroring slightly before you
receive this event.

Keys:

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket.disconnect"``

* ``code`` (*int*) -- The WebSocket close code, as per the WebSocket spec. If no code
  was received in the frame from the client, the server should set this to ``1005``
  (the default value in the WebSocket specification).

* ``reason`` (*Unicode string*) -- A reason given for the disconnect, can
  be any string. Optional; if missing or ``None`` default is empty
  string.


Disconnected Client - ``send`` exception
''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''

If ``send()`` is called on a closed connection the server should raise
a server-specific subclass of ``OSError``. This is not guaranteed, however,
especially on older ASGI server implementations (it was introduced in spec
version 2.4).

Applications may catch this exception and do cleanup work before
re-raising it or returning with no exception.

Servers must be prepared to catch this exception if they raised it and
should not log it as an error in their server logs.


Close - ``send`` event
''''''''''''''''''''''

Sent by the application to tell the server to close the connection.

If this is sent before the socket is accepted, the server
must close the connection with a HTTP 403 error code
(Forbidden), and not complete the WebSocket handshake; this may present on some
browsers as a different WebSocket error code (such as 1006, Abnormal Closure).

If this is sent after the socket is accepted, the server must close the socket
with the close code passed in the message (or 1000 if none is specified).

* ``type`` (*Unicode string*) -- ``"websocket.close"``.

* ``code`` (*int*) -- The WebSocket close code, as per the WebSocket
  spec.  Optional; if missing defaults to ``1000``.

* ``reason`` (*Unicode string*) -- A reason given for the closure, can
  be any string. Optional; if missing or ``None`` default is empty
  string.


WSGI Compatibility
------------------

Part of the design of the HTTP portion of this spec is to make sure it
aligns well with the WSGI specification, to ensure easy adaptability
between both specifications and the ability to keep using WSGI
applications with ASGI servers.

WSGI applications, being synchronous, must be run in a threadpool in order
to be served, but otherwise their runtime maps onto the HTTP connection scope's
lifetime.

There is an almost direct mapping for the various special keys in
WSGI's ``environ`` variable to the ``http`` scope:

* ``REQUEST_METHOD`` is the ``method``
* ``SCRIPT_NAME`` is ``root_path``
* ``PATH_INFO`` can be derived by stripping ``root_path`` from ``path``
* ``QUERY_STRING`` is ``query_string``
* ``CONTENT_TYPE`` can be extracted from ``headers``
* ``CONTENT_LENGTH`` can be extracted from ``headers``
* ``SERVER_NAME`` and ``SERVER_PORT`` are in ``server``
* ``REMOTE_HOST``/``REMOTE_ADDR`` and ``REMOTE_PORT`` are in ``client``
* ``SERVER_PROTOCOL`` is encoded in ``http_version``
* ``wsgi.url_scheme`` is ``scheme``
* ``wsgi.input`` is a ``StringIO`` based around the ``http.request`` messages
* ``wsgi.errors`` is directed by the wrapper as needed

The ``start_response`` callable maps similarly to ``http.response.start``:

* The ``status`` argument becomes ``status``, with the reason phrase dropped.
* ``response_headers`` maps to ``headers``

Yielding content from the WSGI application maps to sending
``http.response.body`` messages.


WSGI encoding differences
-------------------------

The WSGI specification (as defined in PEP 3333) specifies that all strings
sent to or from the server must be of the ``str`` type but only contain
codepoints in the ISO-8859-1 ("latin-1") range. This was due to it originally
being designed for Python 2 and its different set of string types.

The ASGI HTTP and WebSocket specifications instead specify each entry of the
``scope`` dict as either a byte string or a Unicode string. HTTP, being an
older protocol, is sometimes imperfect at specifying encoding, so some
decisions of what is Unicode versus bytes may not be obvious.

* ``path``: URLs can have both percent-encoded and UTF-8 encoded sections.
  Because decoding these is often done by the underlying server (or sometimes
  even proxies in the path), this is a Unicode string, fully decoded from both
  UTF-8 encoding and percent encodings.

* ``headers``: These are byte strings of the exact byte sequences sent by the
  client/to be sent by the server. While modern HTTP standards say that headers
  should be ASCII, older ones did not and allowed a wider range of characters.
  Frameworks/applications should decode headers as they deem appropriate.

* ``query_string``: Unlike the ``path``, this is not as subject to server
  interference and so is presented as its raw byte string version,
  percent-encoded.

* ``root_path``: Unicode string to match ``path``.


Version History
---------------


* 2.0 (2017-11-28): Initial non-channel-layer based ASGI spec


Copyright
---------


This document has been placed in the public domain.

===== content/en/docs/concepts/context-propagation/index.md =====
---
title: Context propagation
weight: 10
description: Learn about the concept that enables Distributed Tracing.
---

With context propagation, [signals](../signals/) ([traces](../signals/traces/),
[metrics](../signals/metrics/), and [logs](../signals/logs/)) can be correlated
with each other, regardless of where they are generated. Although not limited to
tracing, context propagation allows [traces](../signals/traces/) to build causal
information about a system across services that are arbitrarily distributed
across process and network boundaries.

To understand context propagation, you need to understand two separate concepts:
context and propagation.

## Context

Context is an object that contains the information for the sending and receiving
service, or [execution unit](/docs/specs/otel/glossary/#execution-unit), to
correlate one signal with another.

When Service A calls Service B, Service A includes a trace ID and a span ID as
part of the context. Service B uses these values to create a new span that
belongs to the same trace, setting the span from Service A as its parent. This
makes it possible to track the full flow of a request across service boundaries.

## Propagation

Propagation is the mechanism that moves context between services and processes.
It serializes or deserializes the context object and provides the relevant
information to be propagated from one service to another.

Propagation is usually handled by instrumentation libraries and is transparent
to the user. In the event that you need to manually propagate context, you can
use the [Propagators API](/docs/specs/otel/context/api-propagators/).

OpenTelemetry maintains several official propagators. The default propagator
uses the headers specified by the
[W3C TraceContext](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/) specification.

## Example

A service called `Frontend` that provides different HTTP endpoints such as
`POST /cart/add` and `GET /checkout/` reaches out to a downstream service
`Product Catalog` via an HTTP endpoint `GET /product` to receive details on
products that a user wants to add to the cart or that are part of the checkout.
To understand activities in the `Product Catalog` service within the context of
requests coming from `Frontend`, the context (here: Trace ID and Span ID as
"Parent ID") is propagated using the `traceparent` header as it is defined in
the W3C TraceContext specification. This means the IDs are embedded in the
fields of the header:

```text
<version>-<trace-id>-<parent-id>-<trace-flags>
```

For example:

```text
00-a0892f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-f03067aa0ba902b7-01
```

### Traces

As mentioned, context propagation allows traces to build causal information
across services. In this example, the two calls to the HTTP endpoint
`GET /product` of service `Product Catalog` can be correlated with their
upstream calls in service `Frontend` by extracting the remote context from the
`traceparent` header and injecting it into the local context to set the Trace ID
and Parent ID. With that, it is possible in a [backend](/ecosystem/vendors) like
[Jaeger](https://jaegertracing.io) to see two requests as spans of one trace.

![Context propagation example showing trace correlation across services](context-propagation-example.svg)

### Logs

OpenTelemetry SDKs are able to automatically correlate logs with traces. This
means they can inject context (Trace ID, Span ID) into a log record. This not
only enables you to see logs in the context of the trace and span they belong
to, but it also enables you to see logs that belong together across service or
execution unit boundaries.

### Metrics

In the case of metrics, context propagation enables you to aggregate
measurements in that context. For example, instead of only looking at the
response time of all the `GET /product` requests, you can also get metrics for
combinations of `POST /cart/add > GET /product` and
`GET /checkout < GET /product`.

| Name                            | Calls Per Second | Average Response Time |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------- |
| `* > GET /product`              | 370              | 300ms                 |
| `POST /card/add > GET /product` | 330              | 130ms                 |
| `GET /checkout > GET /product`  | 40               | 1703ms                |

## Custom Context Propagation

For most use cases, you will find
[instrumentation libraries or native library instrumentation](/docs/concepts/instrumentation/libraries/)
that handle the context propagation for you. In some cases no such support is
available and you want to create that support for yourself. To do so you need to
leverage the previously mentioned Propagators API:

- On the side of the sender, the context is
  [injected](/docs/specs/otel/context/api-propagators/#inject) into the carrier,
  for example, into the headers of an HTTP request. In other cases, you need to
  find a place that can store metadata for your request.
- On the receiving side, the context is
  [extracted](/docs/specs/otel/context/api-propagators/#extract) from the
  carrier. Again, in the case of HTTP, this is retrieved from the headers. In
  other cases, you pick the place you chose on the sending side to store the
  context.

Note that it is possible to propagate context in protocols that do not have a
dedicated field for metadata, but you have to make sure that on the receiving
side they are extracted and removed before the data is processed, otherwise you
may create undefined behavior.

For the following languages a step-by-step tutorial exists for custom context
propagation:

- [Erlang](/docs/languages/erlang/propagation/#manual-context-propagation)
- [JavaScript](/docs/languages/js/propagation/#manual-context-propagation)
- [PHP](/docs/languages/php/propagation/#manual-context-propagation)
- [Python](/docs/languages/python/propagation/#manual-context-propagation)

## Security best practices

Propagation involves sending and receiving data across service boundaries, which
can have security implications.

### External services

When your service interacts with external services (services you do not own or
trust), consider the following:

- **Incoming context**: Be cautious when accepting context from external
  sources. Malicious actors could send forged trace headers to manipulate your
  tracing data or potentially exploit vulnerabilities in context parsing. You
  might want to ignore or sanitize incoming context from untrusted sources.
- **Outgoing context**: Be mindful of what you propagate to external services.
  Internal trace IDs, span IDs, or baggage items might reveal sensitive
  information about your internal architecture or business logic. You may want
  to configure your propagators to not send context to external or public-facing
  endpoints.

### Baggage

[Baggage](../signals/baggage/) allows you to propagate arbitrary key-value
pairs. Since this data is propagated across service boundaries, avoid putting
sensitive information (like user credentials, API keys, or PII) in baggage, as
it might be logged or sent to untrusted downstream services.

## Support in Language SDKs

For the individual language-specific implementations of the OpenTelemetry API &
SDK, you will find details on the support of context propagation in the
respective documentation pages:

- [C++](/docs/languages/cpp/instrumentation/#context-propagation)
- .NET
- [Erlang](/docs/languages/erlang/propagation/)
- [Go](/docs/languages/go/instrumentation/#propagators-and-context)
- [Java](/docs/languages/java/api/#context-api)
- [JavaScript](/docs/languages/js/propagation/)
- [PHP](/docs/languages/php/propagation/)
- [Python](/docs/languages/python/propagation/)
- [Ruby](/docs/languages/ruby/instrumentation/#context-propagation)
- Rust
- Swift

> [!IMPORTANT] Help wanted
>
> For languages .NET, Rust, and Swift, the language-specific documentation for
> context propagation is missing. If you know any of those languages and are
> interested to help, [learn how you can contribute](/docs/contributing/)!

## Specification

To learn more about context propagation, see the
[Context specification](/docs/specs/otel/context/).

===== Doc/library/subprocess.rst =====
:mod:`!subprocess` --- Subprocess management
============================================

.. module:: subprocess
   :synopsis: Subprocess management.

**Source code:** :source:`Lib/subprocess.py`

--------------

The :mod:`!subprocess` module allows you to spawn new processes, connect to their
input/output/error pipes, and obtain their return codes.  This module intends to
replace several older modules and functions::

   os.system
   os.spawn*

Information about how the :mod:`!subprocess` module can be used to replace these
modules and functions can be found in the following sections.

.. seealso::

   :pep:`324` -- PEP proposing the subprocess module

.. include:: ../includes/wasm-mobile-notavail.rst

Using the :mod:`!subprocess` Module
-----------------------------------

The recommended approach to invoking subprocesses is to use the :func:`run`
function for all use cases it can handle. For more advanced use cases, the
underlying :class:`Popen` interface can be used directly.


.. function:: run(args, *, stdin=None, input=None, stdout=None, stderr=None,\
                  capture_output=False, shell=False, cwd=None, timeout=None, \
                  check=False, encoding=None, errors=None, text=None, env=None, \
                  universal_newlines=None, **other_popen_kwargs)

   Run the command described by *args*.  Wait for command to complete, then
   return a :class:`CompletedProcess` instance.

   The arguments shown above are merely the most common ones, described below
   in :ref:`frequently-used-arguments` (hence the use of keyword-only notation
   in the abbreviated signature). The full function signature is largely the
   same as that of the :class:`Popen` constructor - most of the arguments to
   this function are passed through to that interface. (*timeout*,  *input*,
   *check*, and *capture_output* are not.)

   If *capture_output* is true, stdout and stderr will be captured.
   When used, the internal :class:`Popen` object is automatically created with
   *stdout* and *stderr* both set to :data:`~subprocess.PIPE`.
   The *stdout* and *stderr* arguments may not be supplied at the same time as *capture_output*.
   If you wish to capture and combine both streams into one,
   set *stdout* to :data:`~subprocess.PIPE`
   and *stderr* to :data:`~subprocess.STDOUT`,
   instead of using *capture_output*.

   A *timeout* may be specified in seconds, it is internally passed on to
   :meth:`Popen.communicate`. If the timeout expires, the child process will be
   killed and waited for. The :exc:`TimeoutExpired` exception will be
   re-raised after the child process has terminated. The initial process
   creation itself cannot be interrupted on many platform APIs so you are not
   guaranteed to see a timeout exception until at least after however long
   process creation takes.

   The *input* argument is passed to :meth:`Popen.communicate` and thus to the
   subprocess's stdin.  If used it must be a byte sequence, or a string if
   *encoding* or *errors* is specified or *text* is true.  When
   used, the internal :class:`Popen` object is automatically created with
   *stdin* set to :data:`~subprocess.PIPE`,
   and the *stdin* argument may not be used as well.

   If *check* is true, and the process exits with a non-zero exit code, a
   :exc:`CalledProcessError` exception will be raised. Attributes of that
   exception hold the arguments, the exit code, and stdout and stderr if they
   were captured.

   If *encoding* or *errors* are specified, or *text* is true,
   file objects for stdin, stdout and stderr are opened in text mode using the
   specified *encoding* and *errors* or the :class:`io.TextIOWrapper` default.
   The *universal_newlines* argument is equivalent  to *text* and is provided
   for backwards compatibility. By default, file objects are opened in binary mode.

   If *env* is not ``None``, it must be a mapping that defines the environment
   variables for the new process; these are used instead of the default
   behavior of inheriting the current process' environment. It is passed
   directly to :class:`Popen`. This mapping can be str to str on any platform
   or bytes to bytes on POSIX platforms much like :data:`os.environ` or
   :data:`os.environb`.

   Examples::

      >>> subprocess.run(["ls", "-l"])  # doesn't capture output
      CompletedProcess(args=['ls', '-l'], returncode=0)

      >>> subprocess.run("exit 1", shell=True, check=True)
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        ...
      subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command 'exit 1' returned non-zero exit status 1

      >>> subprocess.run(["ls", "-l", "/dev/null"], capture_output=True)
      CompletedProcess(args=['ls', '-l', '/dev/null'], returncode=0,
      stdout=b'crw-rw-rw- 1 root root 1, 3 Jan 23 16:23 /dev/null\n', stderr=b'')

   .. versionadded:: 3.5

   .. versionchanged:: 3.6

      Added *encoding* and *errors* parameters

   .. versionchanged:: 3.7

      Added the *text* parameter, as a more understandable alias of *universal_newlines*.
      Added the *capture_output* parameter.

   .. versionchanged:: 3.12

      Changed Windows shell search order for ``shell=True``. The current
      directory and ``%PATH%`` are replaced with ``%COMSPEC%`` and
      ``%SystemRoot%\System32\cmd.exe``. As a result, dropping a
      malicious program named ``cmd.exe`` into a current directory no
      longer works.

.. class:: CompletedProcess

   The return value from :func:`run`, representing a process that has finished.

   .. attribute:: args

      The arguments used to launch the process. This may be a list or a string.

   .. attribute:: returncode

      Exit status of the child process. Typically, an exit status of 0 indicates
      that it ran successfully.

      A negative value ``-N`` indicates that the child was terminated by signal
      ``N`` (POSIX only).

   .. attribute:: stdout

      Captured stdout from the child process. A bytes sequence, or a string if
      :func:`run` was called with an encoding, errors, or text=True.
      ``None`` if stdout was not captured.

      stderr will be combined in this attribute, and :attr:`stderr` will be
      ``None``.

   .. attribute:: stderr

      Captured stderr from the child process. A bytes sequence, or a string if
      :func:`run` was called with an encoding, errors, or text=True.
      ``None`` if stderr was not captured.

   .. method:: check_returncode()

      If :attr:`returncode` is non-zero, raise a :exc:`CalledProcessError`.

   .. versionadded:: 3.5

.. data:: DEVNULL

   Special value that can be used as the *stdin*, *stdout* or *stderr* argument
   to :class:`Popen` and indicates that the special file :data:`os.devnull`
   will be used.

.. data:: PIPE

   Special value that can be used as the *stdin*, *stdout* or *stderr* argument

.. data:: STDOUT

   indicates that standard error should go into the same handle as standard

    Base class for all other exceptions from this module.

    .. versionadded:: 3.3
